config.title: Write a timeout wrapper for promises

intro.title: Write a timeout wrapper for promises
intro.body: In this lesson, you will build a function that wraps a promise to add a timeout, ensuring it either resolves with the original promise's result or rejects if it takes too long. You'll learn how to use JavaScript promises, the setTimeout function, and the Promise.race method to handle asynchronous operations with time limits. The main constructs involved are creating promises, managing timeouts, and combining promises to control execution flow. This is a practical skill for making your code more robust by preventing indefinite waiting in network requests or other async tasks.
intro.usecase: In real applications, network requests can hang indefinitely when servers are slow or unresponsive. A timeout wrapper for promises is essential for creating responsive user interfaces like search autocomplete fields, dashboard data fetches, and payment processing forms. For example, when users search in an e-commerce site, you want to show 'Request timed out' after 5 seconds rather than leaving them waiting forever. This pattern also prevents memory leaks in long-running operations and improves overall application reliability.

objectives: Construct a function that accepts a promise and a timeout duration as parameters
Initialize a timeout promise that rejects after the specified duration
Integrate Promise.race() to compete the original promise against the timeout promise
Manipulate the race outcome to return the original promise's value or throw a timeout error
Apply the timeout wrapper to a sample asynchronous operation
Control the timeout behavior by adjusting the duration parameter
Implement error handling to catch and distinguish timeout errors from other promise rejections

steps.title: Import the required Promise APIs
steps.instruction: Create a new JavaScript file and recognize that Promise is a global object available without imports.
steps.hint: In JavaScript, Promise is built into the language and doesn't need to be imported from any module.
steps.analogousExample:
// Promise is globally available
console.log(Promise); // This works without imports
steps.seedCode:
// No imports needed - Promise is a global object

// Your code will go here
steps.expectedOutcome: You'll understand that Promise is a built-in JavaScript object that doesn't require explicit imports.
successCriteria: The code recognizes that Promise is available globally without any import statements.
steps.feedbackCorrect: Great! You've correctly recognized that Promise is a global JavaScript object that doesn't require imports.
steps.feedbackPartial: You're on the right track. Remember that in JavaScript, Promise is built into the language and available globally.
steps.feedbackWrong: Let's clarify: Promise is a built-in JavaScript object that doesn't need to be imported. It's available globally in any JavaScript environment.

steps.title: Define the timeoutWrapper function structure
steps.instruction: Create a function named timeoutWrapper that takes two parameters: promise and timeoutMs. The function should return a new Promise.
steps.hint: You can use either a function declaration or arrow function syntax. The function signature should be (promise, timeoutMs).
steps.expectedOutcome: A timeoutWrapper function is defined with the correct parameters and returns a Promise.
successCriteria: The timeoutWrapper function is defined with two parameters (promise, timeoutMs) and returns a new Promise.
steps.feedbackCorrect: Great! You've correctly defined the timeoutWrapper function structure with the required parameters.
steps.feedbackPartial: You're close. Make sure your function takes two parameters (promise and timeoutMs) and returns a new Promise.
steps.feedbackWrong: The function definition doesn't match the requirements. It should be named timeoutWrapper, take two parameters (promise, timeoutMs), and return a new Promise.

steps.title: Create the timeout promise
steps.instruction: Inside your timeoutWrapper function, create a new promise called timeoutPromise that uses setTimeout to reject with an error after timeoutMs milliseconds.
steps.hint: Use new Promise((resolve, reject) => { ... }) and inside it, call setTimeout(() => { reject(new Error(...)) }, timeoutMs).
steps.expectedOutcome: The timeoutWrapper function now contains a timeoutPromise variable that creates a promise rejecting after the specified timeout.
successCriteria: A timeoutPromise variable is declared inside timeoutWrapper, using new Promise and setTimeout to reject with an Error after timeoutMs.
steps.feedbackCorrect: Great! You've successfully created the timeout promise that will reject after the specified timeout.
steps.feedbackPartial: You're on the right track. Make sure you're creating a new Promise that rejects with an Error inside setTimeout, and the timeout is set to timeoutMs.
steps.feedbackWrong: The timeout promise isn't set up correctly. Remember to create a new Promise that rejects with an Error after timeoutMs milliseconds using setTimeout.

steps.title: Use Promise.race to combine promises
steps.instruction: Inside your timeoutWrapper function, return Promise.race() with the original promise and timeoutPromise as arguments.
steps.hint: Promise.race() takes an array of promises and returns a new promise that settles with the result of the first promise that settles.
steps.expectedOutcome: The timeoutWrapper function now returns Promise.race() with both the original promise and the timeout promise, allowing whichever settles first to determine the outcome.
successCriteria: The timeoutWrapper function returns Promise.race() with the original promise and timeoutPromise as arguments.
steps.feedbackCorrect: Great! You've successfully used Promise.race to combine the original promise and timeout promise. This ensures the wrapper will settle with whichever promise completes first.
steps.feedbackPartial: You're on the right track. Make sure you're returning Promise.race() with both the original promise and timeoutPromise as arguments inside the timeoutWrapper function.
steps.feedbackWrong: The timeoutWrapper function should return Promise.race() with the original promise and timeoutPromise as arguments. Check that you're using the correct syntax for Promise.race().

steps.title: Create a sample promise for testing
steps.instruction: Create a function called delayedResolve that returns a promise resolving after a specified delay.
steps.hint: The function should take a delay in milliseconds and return a new Promise that resolves after that delay using setTimeout.
steps.expectedOutcome: A function named delayedResolve that returns a promise resolving after a given delay.
successCriteria: The delayedResolve function is defined, takes a delay parameter, and returns a Promise that resolves after that delay.
steps.feedbackCorrect: Great! You've created a delayedResolve function that will help test the timeout wrapper.
steps.feedbackPartial: You're close. Make sure delayedResolve takes a delay parameter and returns a Promise that resolves after that delay.
steps.feedbackWrong: The delayedResolve function is not yet defined correctly. It should take a delay and return a Promise that resolves after that delay.

steps.title: Test the timeoutWrapper with a fast promise
steps.instruction: Call timeoutWrapper with a promise that resolves quickly (e.g., 500ms) and a longer timeout (e.g., 1000ms), then log the result.
steps.hint: Use the delayedResolve function to create a promise that resolves after 500ms, then pass it to timeoutWrapper with a 1000ms timeout. Chain a .then() to log the resolved value.
steps.expectedOutcome: The code should create a fast promise (500ms) and pass it to timeoutWrapper with a longer timeout (1000ms), then log the resolved value when it succeeds before the timeout.
successCriteria: timeoutWrapper is called with a promise that resolves in 500ms and a 1000ms timeout, and the result is logged using .then().
steps.feedbackCorrect: Great! You've successfully tested the timeoutWrapper with a fast promise. The promise resolves before the timeout, so the result is logged correctly.
steps.feedbackPartial: You're on the right track, but make sure you're calling timeoutWrapper with a promise that resolves in 500ms and a timeout of 1000ms, and logging the result.
steps.feedbackWrong: Check your implementation. You need to call timeoutWrapper with a promise that resolves quickly (500ms) and a longer timeout (1000ms), then log the result.

steps.title: Test the timeoutWrapper with a slow promise
steps.instruction: Call timeoutWrapper with a promise that resolves slowly (e.g., 2000ms) and a short timeout (e.g., 1000ms), then catch and log the timeout error. Add this test after your existing fast promise test.
steps.hint: Use the delayedResolve function to create a promise that resolves after 2000ms, then pass it to timeoutWrapper with a 1000ms timeout. Use .catch() to handle the timeout error and log it.
steps.expectedOutcome: The test demonstrates that when the promise takes longer than the timeout, the timeoutWrapper rejects with a timeout error.
successCriteria: A call to timeoutWrapper with a slow promise (2000ms delay) and short timeout (1000ms) is added, and the timeout error is caught and logged.
steps.feedbackCorrect: Great! You've successfully tested the timeout scenario. The timeoutWrapper correctly rejects when the promise takes too long.
steps.feedbackPartial: You've added a test, but make sure you're using a slow promise (2000ms) with a short timeout (1000ms) and catching the timeout error.
steps.feedbackWrong: The test for the slow promise scenario is missing or incorrect. Try calling timeoutWrapper with a promise that resolves after 2000ms and a timeout of 1000ms, then catch and log the error.

steps.title: Add error handling for the original promise
steps.instruction: Test the timeoutWrapper function with a promise that rejects before the timeout to verify error propagation. Create a new test case below the existing tests.
steps.hint: Create a new promise that rejects after a short delay, then call timeoutWrapper with it and a longer timeout. Use .catch() to handle the rejection.
steps.expectedOutcome: The timeoutWrapper should correctly propagate errors from the original promise when it rejects before the timeout.
successCriteria: A new test case is added that creates a promise that rejects before the timeout, calls timeoutWrapper with it, and handles the rejection with .catch()
steps.feedbackCorrect: Great! You've successfully tested error propagation. The timeoutWrapper correctly handles promises that reject before timing out.
steps.feedbackPartial: You've added some test code, but make sure you're creating a promise that rejects (not resolves) and calling timeoutWrapper with it.
steps.feedbackWrong: The test case for error handling isn't complete. Create a promise that rejects after a short delay, then test it with timeoutWrapper using a longer timeout.

steps.title: Create a reusable test function
steps.instruction: Create a function called runTests that contains all three test cases and calls them sequentially.
steps.hint: Define a function named runTests that calls timeoutWrapper with each test case and logs the results.
steps.expectedOutcome: A reusable test function that organizes all test cases and can be called to run them.
successCriteria: A function named runTests is defined and contains calls to all three test cases.
steps.feedbackCorrect: Great! You've created a reusable test function that organizes all test cases in one place.
steps.feedbackPartial: You're on the right track. Make sure your runTests function contains all three test cases.
steps.feedbackWrong: Try creating a function called runTests that calls each test case sequentially.

steps.title: Execute the test function
steps.instruction: Call the runTests function to execute all test cases and observe the console output.
steps.hint: Simply write runTests(); at the end of your code to invoke the function.
steps.analogousExample:
// Calling a function to run tests
runTests();
steps.expectedOutcome: After calling runTests(), you should see console output showing the results of all test cases: a fast promise resolving, a slow promise timing out, and a rejecting promise handling errors.
successCriteria: runTests() is called at the end of the code, executing all test scenarios.
steps.feedbackCorrect: Perfect! You've successfully executed the test function. The console output should show all test cases working correctly, demonstrating that your timeoutWrapper handles fast promises, slow promises, and errors properly.
